speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The reason why I filed this Parliamentary Question is arising from a concern expressed by a resident who is a medical professional working in a hospital.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The concern of my resident is that there should be an independent and transparent process of handling feedback, not by the hospital in question, purely because the concern that perhaps the hospital may, in certain circumstances, take the side of the patient rather than the staff.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And also, in addition to that, for more independent tracking and monitoring, whether from a patient point of view or from a staff point of view, there would be more independence if it is done on a centralised and by an independent authority or body, rather than a hospital in question.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: There may be some conflict of interest as well when it comes to that hospital.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I am aware that hospitals do even report perpetrators to the Police for further investigation and take actions against them.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And therefore, there are medical confidentiality issues to allow appropriate judgement on whether that action was something that ought to be taken to task for or if the patient is not compos mentis and he is actually not in the right frame of mind.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If I can just illustrate this, there are three parts to incidence management.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: First, is the immediate response and that involves actually dealing with, sometimes, the patient who is the one causing the harassment or the patient's next of kin.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That has to be something that is dealt with onsite, not by an external third-party.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That is where I made the point earlier about reviewing the medical information behind this.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The circumstances that led to the incident would involve some confidential information about the patient, for example.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have established a new record: 30 minutes of Question Time and we cleared 12 Parliamentary Questions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It goes to show, if supplementary questions and replies are succinct, what we can achieve.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Order of the Day.
